newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares end down 4.36 pct after volatile day.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares end down 4.36 pct after volatile day.

text.p: Dutch shares closed with one of their biggest ever one day losses on Wednesday, as an edgy market wilted under a slew of volatile international influences, dealers said.
The headline AEX index ended 4.36 percent lower, losing 42.64 points to 935.76.

The AEX was knocked at the open by a 100-point fall on Wall Street overnight, opening down around 1.5 percent and dropping through the morning as nervous private investors sold out options positions ahead of Friday's expiries, a dealer said.

The negative tone was reinforced by looming key U.S. retail sales and producer prices data in the afternoon and by the time the reports came in at 1230 GMT, the AEX was languishing some four percent lower.
Benign retail sales, up 0.6 percent in July versus expectations for 0.7 percent, and PPI, which showed a record seventh consecutive decline, briefly inspired a rally.
The Dow spiked up 75 points early, adding impetus and bringing the AEX back inside a one percent loss for the day.
But the recovery slid away into the close, as the dollar skidded against the mark, a broker said.

Dlr/mark broke key support at 1.8380 in the U.S. just ahead of the Amsterdam close, driven by a hawkish Bundesbank monthly report saying the central bank was watching a recent upturn in inflation and would orientate policy towards maintaining price stability.
Dealers said the mood on the market would likely remain somber through the week, with more data to come from the U.S. and technicals looking negative.
"Looks like we're heading towards 900 (points)," one said.
The recent dip in the index had left small investors -- recently the engine of the market -- shellshocked, he said.
The AEX index closed at a new record high of 1010.97 points just three trading days ago.
With attention focused on macro issues, there was little to drive individual stocks, brokers said.

Entertainment group Polygram initially bucked the downtrend in the morning on good news about recent film releases, but was hammered later on to end down 8.80 guilders, 7.38 percent, at 110.50 guilders.
Retailer Ahold was hit by dollar weakness, ending off 3.70 guilders, over five percent, at 55.00. Bank ABN AMRO shed over six percent to 45.20.

U.S. July CPI data due Thursday at 1230 GMT would be closely watched for confirmation that U.S. inflation remained subdued, a trader said, but Wall Street's ambivalence over Wednesday's figures argued for more volatility ahead.
